title: Astro Portal session event payload: target_skipped
description: Records that a planned target was NOT observed, so the journal says so instead of staying silent about it. Emitted by the debriefing for a target marked skipped (or left unticked under `partial`), and by the device in the field when the person gives a target up. It mirrors target_started's identification fields. It is not a verdict on quality and it removes nothing from the plan: the frozen plan still says the target was planned, and this event says the night did not deliver it. `reason` is a deliberately SHORT, closed list so a one-handed tap in the dark stays possible and so later multi-night project statistics can count comparable causes; `notes` carries everything the list cannot. See session-events.md for what this type is for and what it deliberately is not.

targetId.description: The shared catalogue id (as in GET /v1/targets, e.g. "m31") or a plan item's own target reference, when the target resolves to one.

targetLabel.description: A free display name, for a target with no catalogue id — the same label a target_started would have used for the same target.

planItemId.description: Optional: the plan item this target came from, when the session was started from a plan (planner-document.schema.json's plan.items[].id).

reason.description: Optional, and closed: weather — the sky was unusable (cloud, haze, wind, dew, frost); equipment — something in the setup stopped this target (the mount could not reach it, a filter was missing, guiding or power failed); time — nothing went wrong, the night ran out or an earlier target overran; visibility — this target in particular was unavailable (too low, behind a tree, a building or the horizon, or drowned by the Moon); other — anything else, with `notes` carrying the detail. Absent means the person did not say, which is a legitimate and common answer: a target left unticked in a partial debriefing is recorded with no reason at all.
